If you won aboard the brig, GO TO the brig is yours. Otherwise, win or lose, the brig sails on, and your raft is still afloat. GO TO another day at sea.

ev:aux-pirates:crossing-over.html: The brig comes alongside, the grapples bite, and the pirates swing down onto your raft just as you swing up onto their deck. For a moment, everyone stares at everyone else across the gap. Then the pirates scramble back up the ropes, shouting, and you find yourself on a strange, rolling deck, with the whole crew coming at you from every side. Each player draws 1 fewer card in the fight's first round. GO TO Boarding Party.

ev:aux-pirates:pirates.html:
After many long hours of toiling on your improvised vessel, cloth begins to chafe at burnt skin, salt begins to sting against hands made tender by the rope, and the whole ordeal feels even more ridiculous than it seemed ashore.

Suddenly a vessel—a proper one at that, likely a brig—peeks over the horizon, sails billowing in the strong tailwind. You're surprised at your own genuine burst of laughter when you spot yet another source of bad news: a plain black flag hangs from the main mast.

Choose one
  • Wait for them to come alongside, and leap aboard the brig as they leap onto your raft. GO TO crossing over.
  • Retrieve your weapons from dry storage and prepare for battle. GO TO pirates reach you.

ev:aux-pirates:pirates-reach-you.html:
The brig comes alongside, close enough to spit on. Grappling hooks bite into your raft, cutthroats drop onto the logs with knives between their teeth, and archers line the rail above to make sure you stay put.

“Hand over your valuables,” the captain calls down, “and we'll leave you the raft. Probably.”

ev:aux-pirates:the-brig-is-yours.html: The last of the crew go over the side, and swim for your raft, and you're happy to let them have it. You haul down the black flag, and look up at a sky full of sail. GO TO A Ship of Your Own.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:miles-behind-.html: The procession carried you further in one night than you could have walked in two. You and your allies may move up to 2 locations from where you joined it, through terrain that is neither Mountain nor Ocean. STOP READING.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:the-gathered-.html: Coins, beads, a silver comb. Nothing stops you. You gain 12 gold and 1x random Uncommon Travel item. GO TO miles behind you.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:the-offerings.html:
The thread goes slack, and the last of the dead lie down for good. Their offerings are still on the road, glinting in the morning light.

Choose one
  • (+1 curse) Gather the offerings. “They won't be needing them anymore.” GO TO the gathered offerings.
  • Leave the offerings where they lie. GO TO the offerings left.
Whatever the dead found at sunrise, it isn't yours to take. Everyone gains 1 EXP. GO TO miles behind you.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:threadbare.title: Threadbare
ev:aux-procession-of-bones:threadbare.html:
It draws a long grey thread from each sleeve, and two of the crumbled pilgrims pull themselves together again, bone by bone, to see you off the road.

Threadbare
Enemy HP: 8 + 9 per player
Enemy
Raised Bones (#3)
Weaver of Bone (#11)
Outcome
Victory
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

If you won, GO TO the offerings. If you lost, you wake in the grass at noon, alone on an empty road. STOP READING.

ev:aux-procession-of-bones:walking-with-.title: Walking With the Dead
ev:aux-procession-of-bones:walking-with-.html:
You slow your breath until it barely stirs your chest, and fall into step between two pilgrims. Neither turns its head. The road slides away beneath your feet as if the procession carried its own current, and the miles pass without weight or effort.

At dawn the procession halts. Every pilgrim kneels to face the rising sun and lays its offering on the road. At the first touch of light they crumble into the grass, one after another, until only the offerings remain, and the tall figure at the head of the column. It turns, still counting its knuckle beads, and finds it has one pilgrim too many. GO TO Threadbare.

ev:aux-sailing:a-cabin-with-a-window.html: Clean sheets, and the sea going by outside. Rest. When you've rested, GO TO the galleon sails.

ev:aux-sailing:a-good-catch.html: The nets come up silver, and the fisherman pays your share in coin at the next harbour he passes. You gain 3 gold. GO TO the fishing boat sails.

ev:aux-sailing:a-storm.html: For a day and a night, the sea tries to kill you all. By morning it's flat and innocent, and the captain is counting what's left. Discard the top 4 cards of the adventure deck. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:abandon-ship.html: You cast off in the little boat, and the ship sails on without you. Cross out bound for your destination, and take its cube off the map. You're at sea in this sector, in your own boat. GO TO another day at sea.

ev:aux-sailing:aboard-the-fishing-boat.html:
The fisherman hums, and lets out his nets.

Choose one
  • (Discard the top 2 adventure cards) Help him haul the nets, for a share of the catch. GO TO a good catch.
  • Sail on. GO TO the fishing boat sails.
  • (1 gold) Buy the fisherman's skiff, and go your own way. GO TO abandon ship.

ev:aux-sailing:aboard-the-galleon.html:
A bell rings for the change of watch.

Choose one
  • Rest in your cabin. GO TO a cabin with a window.
  • (Everyone loses 3 gold) Dine at the captain's table, and lose your wagers gracefully. GO TO the captain's favour.
  • (Discard the top 2 adventure cards) Drill with the marines. GO TO the marines' drill.
  • Sail on. GO TO the galleon sails.
  • Abandon ship in the ship's boat. GO TO abandon ship.

ev:aux-sailing:aboard-the-merchant-cog.html:
The bosun is shouting at someone, and for once, it isn't you.

Choose one
  • Rest below decks. GO TO below decks.
  • (Discard the top 2 adventure cards) Work the rigging for pay. GO TO an honest wage.
  • Sail on. GO TO the merchant cog sails.
  • Abandon ship in the ship's boat. GO TO abandon ship.

ev:aux-sailing:an-honest-wage.html: The bosun pays in silver, and grudgingly. You gain 3 gold. GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:back-in-pieces.html: The raft comes back to you in pieces. Discard the top 3 cards of the adventure deck. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:below-decks.html: The hammocks sway, the timbers creak, and somebody snores all night. Rest. When you've rested, GO TO the merchant cog sails.

ev:aux-sailing:booking-passage.html:

Active weatherAt the harbour
ThunderstormOnly the galleon sails, at triple the fare
Impenetrable FogOnly the fishing boat sails, feeling its way along the shore, at its usual fare
Choose one
  • (Pay 1 gold for each sector) Take a fishing boat, which keeps close to the shore. GO TO the fishing boat.
  • (Pay 2 gold for each sector) Take a merchant cog. GO TO the merchant cog.
  • (Pay 4 gold for each sector) Take a galleon. GO TO the galleon.
  • Stay ashore. STOP READING.

ev:aux-sailing:the-drowned-king-s-tithe.html:
A grey fog rolls over the ship, and somewhere inside it a bell starts tolling, far below the keel. The sailors go pale. The Drowned King takes a tithe from every ship that crosses his water, they whisper, and they start throwing coins over the side.

  • Keep your gold, and hold your nerve while the bell tolls. GO TO holding your nerve.

ev:aux-saltwind:x-marks-the-spot.title: X Marks the Spot
ev:aux-saltwind:x-marks-the-spot.html:
You pace out the steps from the landmarks on the map, and dig. Under three feet of earth, your spade rings on iron. Inside, on rotten velvet, lies a ring with a ship carved in sea-glass, and under it, wrapped in oilcloth, the captain's own weapon. Turn the ring, and far off, a ship's bell answers. You complete the quest, and you gain 1x random Rare Weapon. You gain Ring of Summon Galleon (Unique Travel #6). You finished The Buried Hoard. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark.

You weren't the only ones with a map. On the next rise, a gang of claim jumpers sit round their fire on a heap of other diggers' chests, watching you. They don't come down: you look like you'd fight for it.

Choose one
  • Go up and take their haul. GO TO Claim Jumpers.
  • Shoulder your chest, and leave them to it. STOP READING.

ev:aux-speak-with-the-dead:speak-with-th.title: Speak with the Dead
ev:aux-speak-with-the-dead:speak-with-th.html:
The dead gather close, and answer whoever is willing to listen.

Choose one
  • Ask about the places they wandered. GO TO the dead remember
  • Ask what waits at the end of the day. GO TO the dead foretell

ev:aux-speak-with-the-dead:the-dead-fore.html: The dead have seen the end of every road. Look at the bottom 3 cards of the adventure deck. You may shuffle it again. STOP READING.

ev:aux-speak-with-the-dead:the-dead-reme.html: They walked these lands long before you, and some of them never stopped. Look at the top two cards of the adventure deck. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:a-frog-in-the-h.title: A Frog in the Hand
ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:a-frog-in-the-h.html: Pip stops blinking, and sits in your hands, fat, green and finally still. For a moment nobody breathes. Then a door creaks open where there was none, and the Magister steps out in his slippers, dressing gown flapping. He takes her in both hands, and his eyes are wet. “Forty years,” he says. “Forty years, and you found her.” He reaches back through the door for a pair of boots, still muddy from places that aren't on any map. “I made these to chase her. Never did catch her. They're yours.” He pats down his dressing gown, and finds two little vials in its pockets as well. You complete the quest, and you gain 2x random Uncommon Potion and Boots of Displacement (Unique Travel #2). You finished Neither Here nor There. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:blink-and-you-l.title: Blink and You'll Miss It
ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:blink-and-you-l.html:
Pip sits in the grass, fat, green and unimpressed, and watches you creep closer. Then she blinks, and there are two of her: one on your left, one behind you. It's the same frog in two places at once, and she has no intention of going home.

Hopping Mad
Enemy HP: 9 + 9 per player
Enemy
Warpfrog (#31)
Additional Rules
  • One more Warpfrog for every 10 curse.
  • At 10 or more curse, enemy HP is 8 + 10 per player; at 20 or more, 12 + 13.
Outcome
Victory
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

If you won, GO TO A Frog in the Hand. If you lost, she watches you limp away, from several directions. STOP READING.

links.clause: If you won

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:here-today.title: Here Today
ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:here-today.html:
A ring of toadstools in the wet grass, and a croak from the middle of it. Or possibly from behind you. Spin the weather vane, and note the number it shows:

VaneNumber
N5
E4
W3
S2

If the number is higher than the number of green cubes on the map, it's Pip: GO TO Blink and You'll Miss It If not, GO TO only a toad

links.clause: If the number is higher than the number of green cubes on the map

ev:aux-the-crooked-spire:only-a-toad.html: It was only a toad, sitting in a patch of flattened grass where something bigger sat not long ago. Remove this green cube. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-humming-vault:countdown.title: Countdown
ev:aux-the-humming-vault:countdown.html:
The counting stops. For a moment there's no sound at all. Then the mountain turns white, and a wall of heat slams into your back. The ground drops away, and you're tumbling through the air, sky and earth swapping places, too stunned to scream. You hit the ground, bounce, and hit it again. When the ringing in your ears fades, you're lying in a ditch a very long way from where you were standing, the coil still clutched to your chest, and the Shackle is already knitting your bones back together.

You complete the quest, the hard way: discard the whole adventure deck, and share out every Exhaustion left in its pile between the players, as evenly as it goes. You finished Cause for Alarm. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark.

The blast throws you straight away from the Vault (if you're on it, you choose the way): move to the land location nearest the spot 4 leagues from the Vault, on the far side of you. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-humming-vault:his-inventions.html:
Most of it is spare parts. Some of it works.

ItemPrice
Tinker's Kit (Common Travel #8)3 gold
Spyglass (Rare Travel #4)12 gold
Dowsing Rod (Rare Travel #5)13 gold
Hang Glider (Rare Travel #2)24 gold

Once you're done trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-humming-vault:hot-pursuit.title: Hot Pursuit
ev:aux-the-humming-vault:hot-pursuit.html:
A buzzing rises behind you, like a hive kicked over. Down out of the sky come brass things on whirring wings, trailing sparks, and they've found you.

Hornets' Nest
Enemy HP: 9 + 9 per player
Enemy
Arc Drone (#44)
Arc Sentry (#8)
Additional Rules
  • With 2 red cubes on the Vault, add a Lodestone Warden, at the left of the line.
  • One more Arc Drone for every 10 curse.
  • At 10 or more curse, enemy HP is 3 + 12 per player; at 20 or more, 9 + 16.
Outcome
Victory
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-humming-vault:out-of-range.title: Out of Range
ev:aux-the-humming-vault:out-of-range.html:
Far behind you, the bells stop. The mountain holds its breath for a long moment, and lets it out again. Whatever was counting has given up on you. You complete the quest. You finished Cause for Alarm. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark.

If a Fate brought you here, read the page equal to your curse. If a rest did, finish your rest. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-humming-vault:the-blast-in-th.title: The Blast in the Night
ev:aux-the-humming-vault:the-blast-in-th.html:
You wake to the counting stopping. Then the mountain turns white, the night turns to noon, and the blast picks up your camp and everyone in it. You come down hard, a long way off, and the Shackle spends the rest of the night knitting your bones.

You complete the quest, the hard way: +2 curse, then finish your rest. You finished Cause for Alarm. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark.

The blast throws you straight away from the Vault (if you're on it, you choose the way): move to the land location nearest the spot 4 leagues from the Vault, on the far side of you. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-humming-vault:the-ornithopter.html: It has four wings, two of them borrowed from a sentry, and it flaps like a startled goose. Somehow, it flies. He shouts directions over the clatter the whole way, most of them wrong. You may move up to 3 locations, ignoring roads and the weather. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-humming-vault:the-tinkerer.html:
The hum has stopped, and somebody has moved into the Vault: a small man in goggles, up to his elbows in a dead sentry. He starts talking before you're through the door, and doesn't stop.

Choose one
  • (Discard the top 4 adventure cards) Hear him out, then ask for a ride in his ornithopter. GO TO the ornithopter.
  • Hear him out, then look over his inventions. GO TO his inventions.
  • Leave. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:a-full-hound.html: She eats it in two bites, and looks at you as if you'd hung the moon. You gain 2 EXP. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:by-his-fire.title: By His Fire
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:by-his-fire.html:
The lord's camp is all firelight, roast venison and sleeping hounds. He waves you to the fire as if you'd been expected.

Choose one
  • (Pay 5 gold) Hire his guide to take the long way round. GO TO the long way round.
  • Drink his wine, and ride on. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:fetch.html:
She's gone a long time. Spin the weather vane:

VaneShe comes back with
N, NEA rabbit, laid at your feet with great ceremony. You gain Beast Meat (Common Travel #10).
NW, E, W, SE, SW, SA different, much larger stick.

STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:horns-in-the-ni.title: Horns in the Night
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:horns-in-the-ni.html: Far off in the dark, horns, and a ragged cheer. In the morning a rider passes with the news: the lord has had his bear. Not the Old Grizzly, it turns out, who slipped them again, but the lord got there first, and he'll be insufferable about it. The quest fails. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:petting-the-hou.title: Petting the Hound
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:petting-the-hou.html:
She leans her whole weight against your legs, and sighs like a bellows.

Choose one
  • (Lose a Beast Meat) Share your supper with her. GO TO a full hound.
  • Throw a stick. GO TO fetch.
  • Leave her to her dreams. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:second-to-the-k.title: Second to the Kill
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:second-to-the-k.html: Horns blare across the woods, then a ragged cheer. When you catch up, the lord is sitting on a dead bear, eating an apple. “Not the old devil himself, sadly: he slipped us again,” he calls. “But I got here first, so I win! Come and lose to me again some time.” The quest fails. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:spoiled.title: Spoiled
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:spoiled.html: By morning the flies have found the bear, and so has the smell. When the lord's huntsmen come out to meet you, they take one look and shake their heads: not even the Old Grizzly, just his mate. The old devil got away again. The quest fails. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:the-haul-home.title: The Haul Home
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:the-haul-home.html:
If you came here from Fate or Sealed Fate, read the Fate section below.

The lord rides up as you're cleaning your blades. He looks at the bears, looks at you, and laughs until he has to be helped off his horse. “First to the kill! But a bear's no trophy rotting in a ravine, friends. Get him to my table before he turns, and we'll call it a hunt.” He wheels his horse for home, his hounds streaming after him, and leaves you the bear.

Setup
  1. Remove the quest's cubes: you carry the Old Grizzly with you. Bring him to the Hunting Manor before you rest.
  2. Move the quest bookmark to this page: The Haul Home is now your active quest, and its effects apply until it ends.
Quest effects
  • When you rest: GO TO Spoiled
Fate (Read this when you play Fate or Sealed Fate)

Read the page equal to your curse, as usual. If it leads to a fight, carrying the bear takes its toll: each player draws 1 card fewer in the first round.

After setting up the quest, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:the-long-way-ro.html: The guide pockets your coin without a word, and in the morning leads his master off down the wrong valley. Move the black cube 1 location back towards the Manor. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:the-old-grizzly.title: The Old Grizzly
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:the-old-grizzly.html:
The trail ends in a ravine full of bones. The Old Grizzly waits at the bottom, grey-muzzled and as big as a cottage, and he isn't alone: a younger bear lumbers out of the shadows beside him. The crows that have followed them for years rise off the bones in a black cloud.

The Old Grizzly
Enemy HP: 9 + 9 per player
Enemy
Towering Beast (#6)
Raven (#14)
Additional Rules
  • One more Raven for every 10 curse.
  • At 10 or more curse, enemy HP is 8 + 10 per player; at 20 or more, 20 + 11.
Outcome
Victory
  • Exquisite Beast Meat (Rare Travel #6).
  • 6 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 8 exp for each player.

If you won, GO TO The Haul Home. If you lost, they let you crawl away. STOP READING.

links.clause: If you won

ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:to-the-lord-s-t.title: To the Lord's Table
ev:aux-the-hunting-manor:to-the-lord-s-t.html:
The whole household turns out to see the Old Grizzly carried in, and the lord tells the story of the hunt before you've finished telling it. Then he sends a servant for something off his trophy wall. You complete the quest, and you gain 1x random Rare Weapon, which he hands over without a second look. You finished The Great Hunt. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark.

“Oh, and that one's yours now,” he adds, nodding at the grey hound from his lodge that has sat down on your foot. “She's decided. I wouldn't argue.” One of you gains Lodge Hound (Unique Travel #4). STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.title: Dead Reckoning
ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.html:
The nearest lid slides aside. A wet skull rises over the edge, followed by a second, then a forest of grasping hands. The dead haul themselves aboard, trailing ribbons and rotten flowers. Apparently the funeral is over.

Unwelcome Passengers
Enemy HP: 10 + 9 per player
Enemy
Raised Bones (#3)
Weaver of Bone (#11)
Outcome
Victory
  • Unless you laid them to rest: 1x random Common Travel item and 4 gold, from the coffins.
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, GO TO another day at sea.

You ease the strap off the branch and retreat with the pack pressed against your chest. Not far enough: the bear lifts its head from the last of the provisions, and finds you between it and its supper. You gain 1x random Common Travel item. Each player draws 1 fewer card in the fight's first round. GO TO The Bear Necessities.

ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.title: The Old Toll
ev:aux-the-last-customer-and-other-fortu.html:
The guards rise with a clatter of loose joints. Their captain taps the empty palm once more, then draws a sword. You appear to have exhausted the available payment methods.

The Old Toll
Enemy HP: 6 + 10 per player
Enemy
Raised Bones (#3)
Inspiring Leader (#40)
Outcome
Victory
  • 4 gold and 1x random Common Weapon, from the toll heap.
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:abandoning.title: Abandoning
ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:abandoning.html: You send your companies back to the camp, and the bands go back to burning. You abandon the quest. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:skirmish.title: Skirmish
ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:skirmish.html:
Smoke on the horizon, and under it, the band: raiders loaded down with loot, and in no mood to give it back.

Scorched Earth
Enemy HP: 13 + 9 per player
Enemy
Bandit (#1)
Marauder (#41)
Additional Rules
  • One more Bandit for every 10 curse.
  • At 10 or more curse, enemy HP is 12 + 9 per player; at 20 or more, 13 + 15.
Outcome
Victory
  • Remove this black cube.
  • Their loot: 1x random Common Weapon and 2 gold.
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

If you won and no black cubes are left, GO TO The Banner Falls. If you lost, you fall back towards your own lines: move 1 location towards your nearest company. STOP READING.

links.clause: If you won and no black cubes are left

ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:the-banner-fal.title: The Banner Falls
ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:the-banner-fal.html:
The warband breaks and scatters into the hills, and its warlord runs with it, leaving his banner trampled in the mud. The marshal's soldiers raise it on a spear, and cheer you until they're hoarse. You complete the quest, and gain 1x random Rare Armor from the marshal's own baggage. You finished Hold the Line. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark.

“Keep it,” says the marshal, handing you the banner. “It's older than the warband, and older than this kingdom too. Whoever fights under it fights like three, and forgets how to be afraid. It's the only thing that held that rabble together.” One of you gains Warlord's Banner (Unique Travel #7). STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:the-camp-at-ea.html:
The camp has the look of an army with nobody left to fight: half the tents are struck, and the soldiers are playing dice in the sun. They still cheer when they see you.

Choose one
  • (Pay 4 gold) Rent a bunk. GO TO a bunk.
  • Visit the quartermaster's sale. GO TO the quartermaster's sale.
  • Leave. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:the-quartermas.html:
The army needs most of what's here, but some of it, he admits, would march off on its own sooner or later.

ItemPrice
Longsword (Common Weapon #1)3 gold
Banded Shield (Common Armor #5)2 gold
Leather Hauberk (Common Armor #3)3 gold

Once you're done trading, STOP READING.

With the war over, the quartermaster would rather sell his stores than carry them home, and he gives the banner's bearer a price.

ItemPrice
Longsword (Common Weapon #1)2 gold
Banded Shield (Common Armor #5)1 gold
Leather Hauberk (Common Armor #3)2 gold
Bardiche (Uncommon Weapon #1)2 gold
Full Helmet (Uncommon Armor #2)3 gold
Tower Shield (Uncommon Armor #5)3 gold

Once you're done trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:the-warlord-s-.title: The Warlord's Host
ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:the-warlord-s-.html:
Your last company breaks, and the bands close on the camp as one host, with the warlord riding at its head under his banner. The marshal's reserves form up behind you, and wait for your order.

Pitched Battle
Enemy HP: 5 + 10 per player
Enemy
Ringleader (#12)
Marauder (#41)
Bandit (#1)
Additional Rules
  • One more Bandit for each black cube still on the map, and one more Marauder for every 10 curse.
  • At 10 or more curse, enemy HP is 4 + 11 per player; at 20 or more, 8 + 14.
Outcome
Victory
  • 6 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 8 exp for each player.

If you won, GO TO The Banner Falls. If you lost, GO TO Withdrawal.

links.clause: If you won
If you lost

ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:withdrawal.title: Withdrawal
ev:aux-the-marshal-s-camp:withdrawal.html: The host burns the camp's outskirts, then melts back into the hills to lick its wounds. It will be back. The marshal is already raising new companies. The quest fails. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:a-blind-eye.html: The coin vanishes, and so does the guard's interest. He has a sudden urge to patrol somewhere else entirely. Remove this black cube. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:a-false-bottom.html: Under the empty vials, the box has a false bottom. In it lies a grey hood, folded small, with a note in silver ink: “For the courier. In this line of work, you'll want eyes in the back of your head.” You complete the quest. You finished Special Delivery. One of you gains Paranoid Watcher (Unique Armor #6). Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:a-sealed-crate.html:
The crates are nailed shut and stencilled with the marks of ships that never reached port. No questions, no refunds. Spin the weather vane:

VaneInside
N, NE1x random Rare item
NW, E, W1x random Uncommon item
SE, SW, SWet straw and one boot

STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:abandoning.title: Abandoning
ev:aux-the-rookery:abandoning.html: You leave the box on a guardhouse step, and walk away fast. You abandon the quest. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:for-the-crown.title: For the Crown
ev:aux-the-rookery:for-the-crown.html:
“Seize that box!” A whistle shrills, and boots come running.

Long Arm of the Law
Enemy HP: 9 + 10 per player
Enemy
Royal Guard (#30)
Protector (#23)
Additional Rules
  • Word has spread: one more Royal Guard for each black cube on the bookmark.
  • One more Protector for every 10 curse.
  • At 10 or more curse, enemy HP is 8 + 10 per player; at 20 or more, 15 + 14.
Outcome
Victory
  • Put this black cube on the bookmark.
  • 6 gold, from the guard's purse.
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

If you lost, GO TO Seized. Otherwise, STOP READING.

links.clause: If you lost

ev:aux-the-rookery:halt.title: Halt!
ev:aux-the-rookery:halt.html:
A guard in the crown's colours steps into the road, hand on hilt. “Papers. And what's in the box?”

Choose one
  • (Pay 5 gold) Bribe the guard. GO TO a blind eye.
  • Fight. GO TO For the Crown.

ev:aux-the-rookery:mother-brine.html:
Mother Brine wears a fox's mask and a great many rings, and she has never once been surprised by anything you could put on her counter. You may sell her any items, for half their value, rounded down. She also sells:

ItemPrice
2x random Uncommon itemItem value

Once you're done trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:seized.title: Seized
ev:aux-the-rookery:seized.html: They take the box, and you with it, as far as the gaol. The Shackle gets you out by morning. The box stays in. The quest fails. Remove the quest's cubes and the bookmark. STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:signed-sealed-deliver.title: Signed, Sealed, Delivered
ev:aux-the-rookery:signed-sealed-deliver.html:
The buyer is a healer, grey with tiredness, in a town that coughs behind every shutter. She breaks the silver wax: medicine, enough for every sickbed in town, that the crown taxes off the roads. The silver mask told you to collect payment. The town has scraped together its last savings to pay it.

Choose one
  • (+1 curse) Take the payment. GO TO the town's savings.
  • Leave it with them. GO TO a false bottom.

ev:aux-the-rookery:the-inner-circle.html:
Behind the inner door, the masks are silk, and the wine is better. The silver mask raises her glass to her courier. Here, the Rookery sells what it doesn't show the street.

ItemPrice
2x random Rare itemItem value

Once you're done trading, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-rookery:the-market.html:
A mask is pressed into your hands at the bottom of the cellar steps. Beyond them, the Rookery: lanterns, smoke and stalls crammed under the old quarter's arches, where foxes, owls and grinning moons haggle in whispers.

Choose one
  • Visit Mother Brine. GO TO Mother Brine.
  • (Pay 10 gold) Buy a sealed crate. GO TO a sealed crate.
  • (If you finished this quest) Knock on the inner door. GO TO the inner circle.
  • Leave. STOP READING.

links.clause: If you finished this quest) Knock on the inner door

ev:aux-the-rookery:the-town-s-savings.html: Nobody meets your eye as you count it. You gain 20 gold. GO TO a false bottom.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:every-bell-in-.html: The djinn smiles for the first time. Gold pours from a clear sky: coins, goblets, a crown or two, clattering across the salt flat like every bell in a cathedral. It's exactly what you asked for. You simply forgot to ask for it quietly. Beneath the nearest dune, something sits bolt upright. You gain 20 gold. Each player draws 1 fewer card in the fight's first round. GO TO The Previous Owner.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:rub-the-lamp.html:
Smoke pours from the spout, far more than the lamp could ever hold, and gathers itself into a figure three times your height. His beard is braided through with brass rings, his eyes glow like banked coals, and he looks exhausted. A heavy iron cuff circles each of his wrists, its chain trailing back into the spout.

He looks you over and sniffs. “Oh. You're one of us.” You follow his gaze to your own wrist. The Shackle is invisible to mortal eyes, but apparently not to his.

“One wish,” he sighs. “The last man to hold my lamp spent the other two. He wished to live forever, and then he wished never to be found.” He points a long finger at the nearest dune. “He's under that one. Still alive, I'm told, so you may want to keep your voice down. Well? Wish.”

Choose one
  • Wish for wealth. GO TO wish for wealth.
  • Wish for power. GO TO wish for power.
  • Wish for the djinn to be free. GO TO wish the djinn free.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:the-previous-o.title: The Previous Owner
ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:the-previous-o.html:
The dune bursts open. The man who wished to live forever claws his way out of the sand, and it's immediately clear that he forgot to wish for anything else. What's left of him is a dry husk in the rags of a king, and the servants buried at his side follow him out. None of them are alive. None of them seem to mind.

“Mine,” he rasps, reaching for the gold with fingers like twigs. “All of it, mine.”

The Previous Owner
Enemy HP: 8 + 9 per player, or 6 + 7 if you freed the djinn: the king is finally dying
Enemy
Raised Commander (#10)
Raised Bones (#3)
Outcome
Victory
  • 1x random Uncommon Travel item: the dead king's crown.
  • If you freed the djinn: 7 gold, from the treasure he took with him.
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • Lose the gold from your wish.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:wish-for-power.html:
“Power.” The djinn nods as if you'd asked for directions. He reaches into the smoke of his own chest and pulls out a weapon still ringing from the forge. As your fingers close around the grip, you feel the Shackle tighten, one link at a time.

“Everything I make is forged from the same stuff as my chains,” he says, not unkindly. “You'll get used to the weight.”

You gain 1x random Uncommon Weapon and 1x random Uncommon Armor, and +1 curse.

The new blade rings as it leaves the smoke, loud as a bell across the salt. Beneath the nearest dune, someone has heard that sound before, and wants to know who's been making wishes without him. GO TO The Previous Owner.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:wish-for-wealt.html: “Wealth,” the djinn repeats, with the weariness of someone who has heard the word ten thousand times. GO TO every bell in a cathedral.

ev:aux-the-shackled-djinn:wish-the-djinn.html:
The djinn stares at you for a long moment. Then he looks down at his wrists, where the iron cuffs have begun to crack like old varnish. “Nobody,” he says quietly, “has ever wasted a wish on me.”

The chains burst into brass dust. The djinn rises, and keeps rising, until he is a pillar of smoke reaching for the clouds, and his voice comes from everywhere at once. “Know this, little shackled one: a djinn's gifts last only as long as his chains. Every wish I ever granted is now unmade. All but this last one, which I intend to keep.”

Beneath the nearest dune, after a great many years, the man who wished to live forever begins to die. He doesn't care to do it quietly. And a man who can finally be found is a man whose treasure can be found, too. GO TO The Previous Owner.

ev:aux-traders:ground-of-your-choosing.html: The tracks lead to a gully where a dozen cutthroats are waiting for dark. You wait for them instead, at the narrow end, where they can only come at you a few at a time. The trader sends two of his guards after you, and promises you his wares if you come back. Each player draws 2 more cards in the fight's first round. GO TO Knives in the Dark.

ev:aux-traders:hired-for-the-night.html: "We are not in business, Shackled," the trader says, and then he chews on it, and on the tracks in the grass. "Stand a watch with my guards, and you can buy what you like at dawn. Touch nothing before then." GO TO Knives in the Dark.

ev:aux-traders:humble-wares.title: Humble Wares
ev:aux-traders:humble-wares.html:
The trader unpacks his wares. "Take a look, though best believe you'll pay anything you touch, in blood or coin." He ponders for a second, before pointing at a nearby guard.

ev:aux-traders:knives-in-the-dark.title: Knives in the Dark
ev:aux-traders:knives-in-the-dark.html:
They come out of the grass without a sound: a cutthroat with soot on his face, and behind him one who moves like smoke, and doesn't seem to be there at all until the knife is.

ev:aux-traders:lightened-purses.title: Lightened Purses
ev:aux-traders:lightened-purses.html:
Tall grass muffles your step as you avoid the dying ember light. As the caravan's guards grunt and banter through their favored games of chance, you find taking the merchant's wares easy as snatching candy from the grasp of a sleeping child. With every one, the Shackle tightens. +1 curse.

You gain 2x random Uncommon item.

You're crouched among the wagons with your arms full when the grass beyond the firelight begins to move. Someone else had the same idea, and brought knives. Each player draws 2 more cards in the fight's first round. GO TO Knives in the Dark.

ev:aux-traders:sword-and-coin.title: Sword and Coin
ev:aux-traders:sword-and-coin.html:
"To me!" the merchant roars as he retreats behind the guardsmen. They draw their swords, falling in practiced formation, blades high in a practiced defensive stance. As you draw, the Shackle tightens. +1 curse.

Fleeing Trader
Enemy HP: 10 + 8 per player
Enemy

Soldier (#22)
Outcome
Victory
  • 1x random Uncommon item, 3x random Common item and 4 gold, from the trader's wares.
  • 4 exp for each player.
Defeat
  • +1 curse.
  • 6 exp for each player.

After resolving the encounter, STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:adrai-l.html: The latch gives under your thumb. Hazy sun rays filter through the trees, and for a moment you feel a peace that carries a hint of the divine. Shackled or not, the occasional stroke of luck isn't yet out of your reach. You gain 1x random Uncommon item and 6 gold. STOP READING.

The marks are Adrai'lalth's, and the statue's stone face is a kind one.

Choose one
  • Take the box. GO TO Adrai'lalth's offering.
  • Leave it for whoever needs it more. STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:shabel-.html: Your body seizes as a dark presence manifests near you: oppressive, ancient and powerful. It appraises you with a gaze that scratches at the edge of your sanity, and the Shackle tightens. When it lets go, you try to scream, but manage only a whimper. The box is gone. In its place lies an artifact of evident power. +1 curse. You gain Shackler's Ankles (Unique Armor #1). STOP READING.

The marks are Shabel's. Whatever this box holds, it wasn't left here out of love.

Choose one
  • Take the box. GO TO Shabel's offering.
  • Leave it well alone. STOP READING.

ev:aux-unidentified-deity-statue:shiny-o.html:
Behind some brambles, you find the source of the glint: an ornate curio box, its latch undisturbed, resting atop an oddly shaped rock. Some abandoned treasure, you'd think, until a second look shows you the rock is no natural formation, but the weathered figure of some deity, arms crossed in an authoritative gesture. The box must be an offering.

Choose one
  • Take the box. "Gods forsook me already, so why be respectful?" GO TO the box taken.
  • (If there is a Gold character in your party) Read the marks on the statue, and learn whose offering it is. GO TO the statue read.
  • Turn around and leave. STOP READING.

You take a closer look and marvel at the quality of the craft; it doesn't take an expert to judge the pieces as very valuable. The hairs standing up on the back of your neck indicate they may carry powerful enchantments as well.

Where some swirl and bubble like oil on the pan, others pulsate lazily in their containers. Labels in minuscule hand list their effects and indications.

Whether or not you trust these potions to behave as they claim, one thing is certain; the store is abuzz with arcane power.

As the black shape retreats into the building, you notice there's more certainty to its gait, and a new ring to the voice with which it sings its happy tune.

It sounds strangely similar to your own voice.

You get on your way, shaking your head in utter confusion.
